record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of fuzzy metric spaces
record.context_brief: Separability of the fuzzy Gromov-Prokhorov space of compact fuzzy mm-spaces.
record.original_question: A compact fuzzy metric-measure space is a quadruple (X, M, *, μ) in which (X, M, *) is a compact fuzzy metric space and μ is a probability measure on X. If one equips the class of all compact fuzzy metric-measure spaces with the fuzzy Gromov-Prokhorov distance M_GP defined via isometric embeddings into a common fuzzy metric space, is the resulting fuzzy metric space separable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that a continuous t-norm is a binary operation $*\colon [0,1]	imes[0,1]	o[0,1]$ that is commutative, associative, continuous, has $1$ as identity, and is non-decreasing in each argument. A fuzzy metric space (in the sense of George and Veeramani) is a triple $(X,M,*)$ where $X$ is a non-empty set, $*$ is a continuous t-norm, and $M\colon X	imes X	imes(0,\infty)	o[0,1]$ satisfies, for all $x,y,z\in X$ and $t,s>0$:
(i) $M(x,y,t)>0$;
(ii) $M(x,y,t)=1$ if and only if $x=y$;
(iii) $M(x,y,t)=M(y,x,t)$;
(iv) $M(x,y,t)*M(y,z,s)\le M(x,z,t+s)$;
(v) the function $t\mapsto M(x,y,t)$ is continuous on $(0,\infty)$.
The family of open balls $B(x,r,t)=\{y\in X : M(x,y,t)>1-r\}$ generates a topology on $X$, and $(X,M,*)$ is called compact if this topology is compact.

A compact fuzzy metric-measure space is a quadruple $(X,M,*,\mu)$ where $(X,M,*)$ is a compact fuzzy metric space and $\mu$ is a Borel probability measure on $X$. Two such quadruples $(X_1,M_1,*,\mu_1)$ and $(X_2,M_2,*,\mu_2)$ (using the same t-norm $*$) are considered equivalent if there is a measure-preserving isometric bijection between the supports of $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$.

For a fuzzy metric space $(Z,N,*)$ and Borel probability measures $
u_1,
u_2$ on $Z$, the fuzzy Prokhorov value at level $t>0$ is
$$P_N(
u_1,
u_2,t)=\sup\{1-\varepsilon : 
u_1(A)\le 
u_2(B(A,\varepsilon,t))+\varepsilon 	ext{ and } 
u_2(A)\le 
u_1(B(A,\varepsilon,t))+\varepsilon\  orall 	ext{ Borel } A\subseteq Z\},$$
where $B(A,\varepsilon,t)=\{z\in Z: \exists a\in A,\ M(z,a,t)>1-\varepsilon\}$.

For two compact fuzzy metric-measure spaces $(X_i,M_i,*,\mu_i)$, $i=1,2$, define the fuzzy Gromov-Prokhorov value
$$M_{GP}((X_1,M_1,*,\mu_1),(X_2,M_2,*,\mu_2),t)=\sup\{P_N(f_{1*}\mu_1,f_{2*}\mu_2,t)\},$$
where the supremum is taken over all fuzzy metric spaces $(Z,N,*)$ and all isometric embeddings $f_i\colon X_i\hookrightarrow Z$ ($i=1,2$).

Let $\mathcal{K}^{	ext{mm}}_*$ denote the class of equivalence classes of compact fuzzy metric-measure spaces with fixed t-norm $*$, equipped with the fuzzy metric $M_{GP}$.

Question: Is the fuzzy metric space $(\mathcal{K}^{	ext{mm}}_*, M_{GP}, *)$ separable?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the list of open problems on fuzzy metric spaces. Searches return only results about the classical (non-fuzzy) Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov space, which is known to be Polish (hence separable), but no published resolution of the fuzzy analogue was found. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A note on the Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov distance between (locally) compact metric measure spaces
status_evidence.snippet: The Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov metric on compact metric measure spaces yields a Polish (hence separable) space.
status_evidence.claim: The classical analogue is known to be separable, but no fuzzy-version result was located, suggesting the fuzzy case remains open.

status_evidence.snippet: Question 3. Is the obtained fuzzy metric space of all compact fuzzy mm-spaces separable? Is it completable?
status_evidence.claim: The separability question for the fuzzy Gromov-Prokhorov space is stated as an open problem.
